description: A graduate course on the reasoning side of AI: search at scale, constraint and logic solvers, automated planning, probabilistic and symbolic knowledge, and agents built on foundation models. Students implement solvers and planners, visualise their search behaviour, and finish with a small research-style project.
modelledOn: Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
Ghallab, Nau and Traverso, Automated Planning and Acting
Biere et al., Handbook of Satisfiability
Koller and Friedman, Probabilistic Graphical Models
outcomes: Analyse and implement heuristic, adversarial and sampling-based search, and explain their optimality and complexity guarantees.
Model problems as constraint satisfaction, SAT or SMT instances and explain how modern solvers prune the search space.
Formulate planning domains in PDDL and compare state-space, relaxation-based and hierarchical planners.
Perform exact and approximate inference in probabilistic models and make decisions by maximum expected utility.
Build and query a knowledge graph with ontologies, and explain how symbolic and neural methods can be combined.
Design, test and critique a tool-using foundation-model agent, and report a small experiment with ablations.

units.title: Search at scale
topics: A* optimality, admissible and consistent heuristics, pattern databases
IDA*, beam search and memory-bounded search
Local search: hill climbing, simulated annealing and genetic algorithms
Monte Carlo tree search and the UCT rule
Alpha-beta pruning, move ordering and transposition tables
Stochastic and imperfect-information games; counterfactual regret minimisation

units.title: Constraint satisfaction and SAT/SMT solving
topics: CSP formulation, backtracking with MRV, and arc consistency (AC-3)
Global constraints, symmetry breaking and min-conflicts local search
Propositional SAT: CNF, DPLL and unit propagation
Conflict-driven clause learning: watched literals, restarts and VSIDS
SMT: theories of arithmetic, arrays and bit-vectors; DPLL(T)
Applications: timetabling, configuration and bounded verification

units.title: Automated planning
topics: STRIPS and PDDL; state-space versus plan-space planning
Delete-relaxation heuristics (h-add, h-FF) and landmarks
Graphplan and planning as satisfiability
HTN and temporal planning; replanning and execution monitoring

units.title: Probabilistic reasoning and decision theory
topics: Bayesian networks, d-separation and exact inference by variable elimination
Approximate inference: likelihood weighting, Gibbs sampling and particle filters
Hidden Markov models and dynamic Bayesian networks
Utility theory, decision networks and the value of information
Markov decision processes: value iteration and policy iteration

units.title: Knowledge graphs and ontologies
topics: RDF triples, RDFS, OWL and SPARQL queries
Description logics: subsumption, consistency and tableau reasoning
Knowledge graph embeddings and link prediction (TransE style)
Building graphs from text: entity linking and relation extraction
Domain ontologies for African health and agriculture; quality and bias

units.title: Neuro-symbolic methods
topics: Limits of purely neural and purely symbolic systems
Logic as differentiable constraints: fuzzy logic and logic tensor networks
Probabilistic logic programming and Markov logic
Learned heuristics for search, SAT and planning
Neuro-symbolic concept learning and visual reasoning
Evaluation: systematic generalisation and explainability

units.title: Foundation-model agents
topics: Language models as policies: prompting and reason-act loops
Tool use, function calling and retrieval-augmented generation
Agent memory, planning and reflection; pairing a model with a classical planner
Multi-agent orchestration and debate
Evaluating agents: benchmarks, failure modes, hallucination and cost
Safety, misuse, sandboxing and guardrails

units.title: Research project
topics: Choosing a problem, baselines and a hypothesis
Experimental protocol, ablations and statistical reporting
Writing a conference-style report and reviewing a peer report
Reproducibility and open problems in reasoning systems

schedule.title: Heuristic and local search
schedule.exercise: Prove that a consistent heuristic is admissible, build a pattern database heuristic for the 8-puzzle, and compare A*, IDA* and beam search by nodes expanded and memory used.

tasks.title: Run A* on an 8-puzzle with Manhattan distance and misplaced-tile heuristics and compare nodes expanded and solution length for five start states
Implement IDA* and beam search for the 15-puzzle, then compare memory, nodes expanded and solution quality on ten instances
Solve a 50-city travelling salesman instance with simulated annealing and a genetic algorithm, tuning cooling and mutation to compare tour length and runtime

schedule.title: Adversarial and sampling-based search
schedule.exercise: Show how move ordering changes alpha-beta node counts, explain the UCT selection rule, and compute one round of counterfactual regret minimisation on a small matrix game.

tasks.title: Run alpha-beta on a game tree with and without move ordering and count the pruned nodes in each run
Implement Monte Carlo tree search with UCT for tic-tac-toe, play 200 games against a random player and report the win rate against the iteration budget
Implement regret matching for rock-paper-scissors with an exploitable opponent and show the average strategy converging to the equilibrium over 10,000 rounds

schedule.title: Constraint satisfaction and basic SAT
schedule.exercise: Model a school timetable as a CSP, apply AC-3 by hand to a small map-colouring instance, and run DPLL with unit propagation on a ten-clause formula.

tasks.title: Colour the regions of Ghana with four colours as a CSP, applying AC-3 and MRV, and record each domain reduction and backtrack
Solve 8-queens and a 20-queen instance with backtracking and min-conflicts, comparing steps taken, and add a symmetry-breaking constraint to cut the search
Implement DPLL with unit propagation and pure literal rules, then measure its runtime on random 3-SAT near the 4.26 clause ratio

schedule.title: Clause learning, SMT and applications
schedule.exercise: Explain on a small conflict how clause learning produces a new clause and a backjump, and encode a lecture timetable with room, lecturer and time constraints as an SMT problem.

tasks.title: Trace a CDCL solver on a small formula, writing down each decision, propagation, conflict, learned clause and backjump level
Encode a 4x4 Sudoku and a small exam timetable as SAT clauses, solve them with a provided solver and check every constraint
Express a bounded loop property over bit-vectors as an SMT query, find a counterexample for an overflow bug and prove the fixed version safe

schedule.title: Classical and hierarchical planning
schedule.exercise: Write a PDDL domain for delivering medicines between clinics by truck, compute the h-FF value of its start state, and decompose the task as an HTN method set.

tasks.title: Write STRIPS operators for a blocks world, then step a forward search to find a plan for a four-block goal and list the states visited
Compute the h-add and h-FF values of an initial state by building the relaxed planning graph, and compare them with the true plan length
Encode a six-step logistics plan as a SAT problem with fixed horizon, solve it, and find the shortest horizon that yields a plan

schedule.title: Bayesian networks and inference
schedule.exercise: Build a Bayesian network for malaria diagnosis from symptoms and test results, answer three queries with variable elimination, and run particle filtering on a hidden Markov model.

tasks.title: Compute the posterior probability of malaria given fever and a positive rapid test in a five-node network using variable elimination
Estimate a posterior with likelihood weighting and Gibbs sampling, then plot error against sample count and compare with the exact answer
Implement a particle filter to track a hidden state in a noisy sensor model, and compare its error with the exact forward algorithm over 200 steps

schedule.title: Decision networks and MDPs
schedule.exercise: Compute the expected utility of three crop-planting actions under uncertain rainfall, the value of perfect information, and solve a 4x3 grid MDP by value and policy iteration.

tasks.title: Compute the expected utility of three planting decisions under two rainfall states and the value of perfect weather information
Run value iteration on a 4x3 grid world with noisy moves and show the value table and policy at iterations 1, 5 and convergence
Compare value iteration with policy iteration on a 100-state random MDP across discount factors and report iterations and runtime to a fixed tolerance

schedule.title: Knowledge graphs and ontologies
schedule.exercise: Model crops, diseases and treatments for Ghanaian farmers as an OWL ontology, query it with SPARQL, and discuss whose knowledge the graph includes and omits.

tasks.title: Write 20 RDF triples about crops and pests, load them in a query engine and answer four SPARQL queries with filters
Add class axioms to the crop ontology, run a reasoner to infer new subclass and type facts, and find one logical inconsistency
Train a small TransE embedding on a 200-triple graph, hold out 20 triples and report mean rank and hits at 3 for link prediction

schedule.title: Why combine neural and symbolic methods
schedule.exercise: Collect three tasks where a neural net alone fails and three where a rule system alone fails, then write a fuzzy-logic rule as a differentiable loss and a small ProbLog program.

tasks.title: Train a small network on an arithmetic-rule task, test it on out-of-range inputs and record where it fails while a rule system succeeds
Add a differentiable logic penalty for a rule such as mutual exclusion to a classifier loss, and compare rule violations before and after
Write a probabilistic logic program for a disease spread network, query marginals and compare them with a hand-built Bayesian network

schedule.title: Learned search and neuro-symbolic evaluation
schedule.exercise: Compare a learned heuristic with a hand-crafted one in the 15-puzzle, and write a short critique of a published neuro-symbolic result, covering what the generalisation test does and does not show.

tasks.title: Train a small network to predict distance-to-goal on 8-puzzle states and use it as the heuristic in A*, comparing node counts
Build a pipeline that extracts shapes from small images with a neural classifier and answers counting questions with a symbolic program
Test systematic generalisation by training on short compositions and testing on longer ones, and report the accuracy drop for neural and hybrid models

schedule.title: Language model agents and tools
schedule.exercise: Design a reason-act agent that answers questions about a market-price database using a search tool and a calculator, and decide when to hand planning to a classical planner.

tasks.title: Write a reason-act loop with a scripted model stub that calls a calculator tool, and log each thought, action and observation
Build a retrieval step over 50 short documents, wire it into an agent and measure answer accuracy with and without retrieval
Have a language model produce PDDL for a delivery task, validate it with a planner and compare success against free-form step lists

schedule.title: Multi-agent systems, evaluation and safety
schedule.exercise: Evaluate an agent on twenty tasks, classify its failures, estimate cost per success, and write a threat model for its tools covering prompt injection and data leaks.

tasks.title: Run an agent on 20 scripted tasks, record success and failure type for each, and tabulate failure categories with their counts
Orchestrate a planner, a worker and a checker agent on a small task set and compare success against a single agent
Craft five prompt-injection attacks against a tool-using agent, measure how many succeed, then add guardrails and report the remaining failures

schedule.title: Project, ablations and open problems
schedule.exercise: Present a four-page report on a small research question with a baseline, ablations and error bars, and review a peer's report using a conference rubric.

tasks.title: Pick a reasoning task, implement a simple baseline and report its score on a fixed test set with the exact setup recorded
Run an ablation of two components over five random seeds and report mean results with standard deviations for each configuration
Re-run a classmate's experiment from their report alone, document any missing details and compare your numbers with theirs
